recommendation: After baseline stage and real allocator-count diagnosis, first evaluate one domain-owned spare lease std::map::node_type. It removes a recurring node allocation/free pair rather than only changing comparisons or hints.

cost_structure.current: Each owner uses an allocations map node. Each lease acquire/release uses another leases map node; owner release while borrowed retains the allocation node until last lease release. The small trace has a batch of live owners but normally one active lease at a time.
cost_structure.predicted_reduction_not_measured: Within a serial 32-owner batch, one spare lease node can serve 32 lease cycles after the first lease node creation: 31 subsequent lease metadata allocations and their matching frees can be avoided, while one node is released at collect/trim. Actual implementation heap-count evidence remains required.
cost_structure.allocation_pool_caveat: A prepared-single batch creates all owners before their release, so allocation-node recycling within that batch has no opportunity. Pooling allocation nodes first may add cold setup and retention without benefiting this trace.

minimal_shape.declaration: using LeaseMap = std::map<u64, Lease>; LeaseMap leases; LeaseMap::node_type spare_lease;
minimal_shape.acquire: Keep all validation and take_id under the existing domain mutex. If spare is empty use the existing emplace path. Otherwise move the spare into a local node handle, replace key with the fresh ID, overwrite mapped Lease, and insert the node into this same leases map. Update reader/writer counts and publish out only after insertion.
minimal_shape.release: After locating the live lease and updating its allocation counts as today, extract(iterator) into spare if spare is empty; otherwise erase(iterator) as today. Continue owner retirement and backing cleanup unchanged.
minimal_shape.cleanup: In reclaim_all, after the provider_poisoned guard and before detach/unlock/callbacks, reset spare to an empty node_type. The trim/collect callers have already required quiet. Arena reset intentionally retains the spare for reuse. Destruction provides a final RAII release.
minimal_shape.no_extra_policy: One spare is a hard cap on idle lease nodes, no vector/free-list allocation or production dependency. Do not add map insertion hints or notification gating to this candidate.

invariants: next_id initializes once, increments under domain mutex, never resets on Arena reset, and stops before overflow; replacing a detached node key with the new ID does not recycle a public handle.
All lease map and spare handle operations use the same domain mutex. Releasing from another thread is serialized exactly like the existing map erase path.

The cache node is extracted from, and reinserted into, the same domain leases map. Its allocator is therefore equal to the target allocator; production std::allocator is always equal. Do not transfer a node between the allocations and leases map types or between domains.

An extracted node is no longer an active lease: leases.size(), quiet, and snapshot active_leases must continue to consider only the map, not the spare. Its old mapped allocation ID is inert and overwritten before reinsertion.

Lease contains only an allocation ID and writer flag, so a cached node owns no backing, external context or provider lifetime. Caching does not retain external buffers or bypass read-only permission checks.

Owner release with outstanding readers/writer still increments retiring bytes and preserves allocation/backing exactly as before. Last lease release still consumes its allocation metadata and returns standalone backing when appropriate.
The empty map sentinel remains owned by the map. Destroying the separate spare handle frees only an extracted node, unlike releasing the underlying resource of a still-live empty pmr map.

Unknown external/provider callback outcomes retain claims and budget as before. A poisoned domain that cannot collect/destroy may additionally retain at most one idle lease node; it must not be described as leak freedom.
The public domain type is opaque; an additional node_handle field changes internal domain size, not the public C ABI or C++ wrapper layout. No new capability bit or API is needed.
exception_and_ownership: Default-empty node_handle needs no node allocation. extract(iterator) transfers node ownership and preserves the original allocator; it does not construct a new node.

insert(node_type&&) reuses the existing node but can still perform comparisons or max_size checks. A local node handle remains the RAII owner if insertion throws; discarding optional cached storage is safe, and the original guard maps errors as before.
Reader/writer counters and output handles remain after successful insertion. A failed insertion therefore publishes no lease and consumes no new logical ownership, just as failed emplace does today.

Duplicate keys are unreachable from the existing strictly increasing ID invariant. Do not add speculative duplicate-key recovery machinery; the same invariant already makes ignored emplace duplicate results safe in baseline.
Resetting a spare node to node_type{} deallocates it through its original allocator. No cache-path allocation is required on release or quiet trim/collect.
CountingAllocator diagnostic state must outlive the cached handle allocator copy. Put counter/resource state before maps/cache members so reverse destruction releases cache and maps first.

memory_and_budget.retention_bound: At most one idle lease node plus one node_handle field per domain; live map nodes remain unchanged. Exact bytes depend on MSVC/libc++ and build mode and must be measured rather than copied from a guessed size.
memory_and_budget.cold_cost: A default-empty handle adds internal domain storage but no heap cache allocation. The first lease still allocates one node; later compatible lease cycles can reuse it.
memory_and_budget.pressure_release: quiet trim and collect clear the spare before provider callbacks. Arena reset keeps it because reset already retains Arena storage.
memory_and_budget.accounting: mgmem_snapshot_v1.backing_bytes explicitly excludes metadata and RSS. Preserve its budget meaning; report the bounded metadata retention separately and do not claim zero resident memory from CLOSED_ZERO or fewer allocator calls.
memory_and_budget.rss: The CRT/OS may already cache freed nodes. Eliminating allocator calls proves work reduction only; lower RSS, energy or product latency are not implied.

alternatives.assessment: C++17 standard-only and mutex serialization fit, but chunks retain a potentially large peak. Calling release while an empty map is alive can invalidate an allocator-owned sentinel on MSVC. Safe pressure release needs destroying/reconstructing maps and explicit reconstruction failure handling, so it is a larger first step.

Can bound cached blocks and keep map APIs, but adds alignment, rebind, node-size buckets, destruction and matching-deallocation machinery. Prefer a standard node handle for the first isolated structural change.

Could remove tree searches and amortize allocations, but monotonically increasing public IDs cannot directly index a permanently growing vector. Recycling slots requires ID-to-slot/generation logic, stable-address and rollback design across callbacks. This is substantially broader than one bounded node cache.

Can remove the second allocation-map lookup on release because leases keep allocation metadata alive, but it changes internal references and needs independent lifetime/exception audit. It does not remove the recurring lease-node allocation/free pair and should not be mixed into this candidate.

meaningful_validation_after_diagnosis: Actual CountingAllocator node counts: empty baseline sentinel counts separately; serial multi-lease cycles allocate one lease node then reuse; simultaneous live leases still have distinct nodes; trim/collect release the spare.
Fresh-ID and stale-handle checks after reuse, including cross-thread read/write lease release and an external imported region.
Existing owner/lease close, callback failure/quarantine, budget and reset/trim contracts; selected-source host and ASan gates.
Compare staged cost diagnostics and unchanged existing main/tiny/prepared-single paired workloads; retain cold/close and concurrent reverse cases and memory-retention evidence.
